scenario_summary: Customer is seeking a refund for a service canceled 34 days ago, which is outside the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Imani Robinson and I'm 31. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?
Okay, I see. Can you give me your account number so I can look that up?
Thanks. And what was the name of the service you're talking about again?
It's the Premium Monthly Subscription I mentioned in my account notes when I requested the cancellation.
Right. Well, our policy is 30 days, and since you're at 34 days, I can't really do anything here. It's just our policy.
I understand the policy, but given the circumstances, is there no exception or a manager I could speak with?
Look, I'm just following the rules here. I'll go ahead and send this to the billing department, but they probably won't do anything either. I've opened a ticket for them to look at it.

escalation_reason: Agent lacked confidence in policy exceptions and pushed the decision to the billing department rather than resolving or denying it directly.

judge_scores.justification: The agent verified the account efficiently but displayed a dismissive tone by failing to genuinely acknowledge the customer's travel circumstances. Furthermore, the agent showed minimal resolution effort by immediately deflecting the issue to the billing department with a pessimistic attitude rather than attempting to properly handle or evaluate the exception request within their authority.
